overview: The Cholas of the Kaveri delta, restored under Vijayalaya in 848, ruled the Tamil south for four centuries and sent fleets across the Bay of Bengal. Their bronze Natarajas, the great temples of Thanjavur and Gangaikonda Cholapuram and their village assemblies are the high point of Tamil civilization.

items.text: Rajaraja I finished the Brihadisvara temple at Thanjavur, its granite tower about 66 meters high.
Bronze images of Shiva Nataraja, cast by the lost-wax method, reached their classic form in the tenth and eleventh centuries.
Rajendra I sent a fleet against Srivijaya in 1025 and sacked its ports along the Strait of Malacca.
Merchant guilds such as the Ayyavole Five Hundred traded across the Indian Ocean, and Chola embassies reached Song China in 1015 and 1077.
Tanks, sluices and the Kaveri's old anicuts irrigated the delta's rice fields.
Ocean-going ships carried armies to Sri Lanka, the Maldives and Sumatra.
Village assemblies chose their committees by lot from eligible landholders, as the Uttaramerur inscriptions of the 920s record.
The Great Living Chola Temples were listed by UNESCO.
Chola bronzes and temple styles were carried to Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia.

fall.text: The Pandyas of Madurai defeated the Cholas repeatedly from the 1210s and absorbed the last of the kingdom by 1279.
